chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleym al-Farra', who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'An-nurah is a cleanser (purifier).'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.النُّورَةُ: Lime paste, a mixture of lime and water used for whitewashing, often discussed in fiqh regarding ritual purity.
key_terms.طَهُورٌ: A purifier or cleanser, indicating that the substance removes impurity or is itself pure.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the purity of lime paste (an-nurah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the legal status of 'an-nurah' (lime paste) as 'tahoor', signifying its ritual purity for use in ablution or general cleansing. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh for determining the permissibility of using common building materials in acts of worship, reflecting the practical application of purity laws in daily life. The brevity of the narration highlights the definitive nature of the Imam's declaration on the substance's intrinsic cleanliness.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, form Suleym Al Fara’a who said,
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Al-Noura is a cleanser’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sulaym al-Farra’ who has said the following: “’
Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, Time is a cleansing (agent).”’
